extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners participating in USPTO inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for handling submissions, defects, timing, and parties' rights in USPTO inter partes reexamination proceedings. Covers examiner options, notice forms, page limits, and third-party/patent-owner interaction rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party forfeiture of comments on a response not commented upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third party requester elects not to file comments on a particular patent owner response, comments on that response will be refused consideration; the failure to file comments applies only to the specific response which the third party requester elects not to comment upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third party requester does not lose rights to comment on future patent owner responses. Where a response was determined incomplete, see exceptions for comments on completed responses (MPEP § 2666.40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party may comment on completed patent-owner responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner did not file comments on a response that was determined by the Office to be incomplete, the third party requester may file comments on the response once it is completed (by patent owner’s submission of a supplemental response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response as completed is treated as a new response on-the-merits and the third party requester is entitled to 30 days to file comments. Exception: where only a fee (other than an excess claims fee) is needed to complete the response, the third party may not file comments after the fee is submitted; see MPEP § 2666.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to timely appeal by third party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the third party requester fails to make a timely appeal or the third party requester’s appeal is dismissed, the third party requester loses further rights as the appellant in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent owner appellant continues its appeal, the third party requester as respondent can file a respondent brief and can enter the appeal pursuant to 37 CFR 41.77(c) and (e). The third party requester can also comment on any subsequent patent owner response to any Office action issued after the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination when no appeal pending after requester fails to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the third party requester fails to timely appeal, or the requester’s appeal is dismissed, and no other appeal is pending in the proceeding, the prosecution of the reexamination proceeding should be terminated by the issuance of a NIRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when no other appeal keeps prosecution open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive patent-owner submission (37 CFR 1.957)
rubrics_metrics.description: A response by the patent owner will be considered not fully responsive to a non-final Office action where a bona fide response is filed before expiration but, through apparent oversight or inadvertence, some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation the prosecution should not be terminated automatically; the examiner may (A) waive non-serious deficiencies and act on the submission, or (B) treat the amendment/response as incomplete and notify the patent owner to complete the response within a set period (37 CFR 1.957(d)) to avoid termination (1.957(b)) or limiting prosecution to patentable claims (1.957(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option A — waive minor deficiencies and act on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent owner submission is a bona fide attempt to advance the reexamination but contains a minor deficiency (e.g., fails to treat every rejection, objection, or requirement), the examiner may simply act on the amendment and issue a new Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new Office action may reiterate the unaddressed rejection/objection/requirement or indicate it is no longer applicable; examiner should identify the part of the previous Office action which was not responded to and clearly indicate what is needed. Not appropriate for serious deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option B — notify of serious deficiency and require completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner’s submission contains a serious deficiency and the period for response has expired (or insufficient time remains), the patent owner should be notified of the deficiency and given a new time period (usually 1 month) pursuant to 37 CFR 1.957(d) to supply the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the omission is not supplied within the new period (or any extension under 37 CFR 1.956), consequences under 37 CFR 1.957(b) or (c) will result (termination or limiting prosecution). Form paragraph 26.06 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 26.06 — Submission Not Fully Responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: Form text notifying that the communication filed is not fully responsive; states the response appears bona fide but consideration of some matter or compliance with some requirement has been omitted and patent owner is required to supply the omission or correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a shortened statutory period to expire ONE MONTH, or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer), from mailing date (or after due date for response to last Office action, whichever is longer). Examiner notes: explain omitted matter in bracket 2 and clearly indicate what is needed; not for deliberate omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No telephone notification — interviews prohibited in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner cannot simply be notified by telephone that the omission must be supplied within the time period for the remaining response; that would be an interview, and interviews are prohibited in inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.955).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be in writing (form paragraph or other written notification action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent omission rules and limits on repeated notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of giving the patent owner a time period to supply an omission (pursuant to 37 CFR 1.957(d)) applies only where the missing matter is considered by the examiner as being 'inadvertently omitted.' Once an inadvertent omission is brought to the patent owner’s attention, inadvertence no longer exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second written notification giving another new (1 month) period is generally not appropriate unless the patent owner’s response raises a different issue of a different inadvertently omitted matter. Examiner may decline to follow practice if abuse is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner completion of response and third party comment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases the patent owner will have 30 days or one month (whichever is longer) to complete the response. After the owner completes the response, the examiner will wait two months from the date of service of the patent owner’s completion and then take up the case for action, since the 30 days for the third party requester comments will have expired by that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The completed response is treated as a new response on-the-merits; the third party requester is entitled to respond and has 30 days to do so whether or not the third party filed comments on the incomplete response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-only completion limitation on third party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If only a fee is needed for the patent owner to complete the response (other than a failure to pay excess claims fees), any third party requester comments must be filed within 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s original (incomplete) response; the third party is not permitted to file comments in response to the submission of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a fee alone adds nothing on the merits (example: terminal disclaimer filed but fee omitted). However, if the patent owner’s response also includes argument (not just a fee), the third party can comment since merits have been addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fee exception for comment rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a failure to pay an excess claims fee by the patent owner, the third party requester does not have the new claim 'package' to comment on; thus, third party requester comments may be filed within 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s response correcting the excess claims fee deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the patent owner corrects the excess claims fee deficiency, claims come into existence in the proceeding and third party comments become relevant and will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective (informal) submission examples (PTOL-2069 defects A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the substance of a submission is complete, the submission can be defective (an 'informal submission'). Defects include: (A) paper filed does not include proof of service; (B) paper filed is unsigned; (C) paper signed by a person who is not of record; (D) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-2069 is used to notify parties of these defects; if additional clarification needed, include separate sheet. If defect not among listed boxes, check 'Other' and explain. Example: submission on easily erasable paper would be unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form PTOL-2069 and correction period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission is defective (informal), form PTOL-2069 is used to provide notification of the defects present. A time period of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) from the mailing date of the PTOL-2069 letter will be set for correcting the defect(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner may request an extension under 37 CFR 1.956. The third party requester is barred from requesting an extension by statute (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2)). If the defect is not corrected, the submission will not be entered; failure to correct resulting in failure to file a timely response may lead to termination or limitation under 37 CFR 1.957.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA may correct obvious defects before examiner action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the defect in the patent owner response or third party comments is limited to an obvious problem (signature, claim format, or other easily corrected defect) and noted by OPLA processing staff, OPLA may issue form PTOL-2069 to notify parties and obtain a response prior to forwarding the case to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise, responsibility lies with the examiner to obtain needed corrections; defects may be identified to examiner by OPLA memo or noted independently by examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of correcting a defective submission that also contains merits discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission correcting a defect provides a discussion of the merits, that discussion should (A) be set forth separately from the portion correcting the defect, and (B) clearly identify the additional discussion as going to the merits. The additional discussion must itself have an entry right or the entire submission will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If merits portion is not clearly delineated, entire submission may be returned and one additional opportunity (30 days or one month, whichever longer) will be provided to correct the defect without a discussion of the merits. Examiner may, however, choose to permit entry of such a paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized or inappropriate papers will not be considered (37 CFR 1.939)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unauthorized paper is filed by any party at any time during the inter partes reexamination proceeding it will not be considered and may be returned. Unless otherwise authorized, no paper shall be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits of the inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence may be entered and considered, entered but not considered, or not entered and returned. If an inappropriate paper was already scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) it cannot be physically returned but can be expunged (marked non-public and closed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of papers returned — patent owner premature filings and petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature responses/comments by the patent owner (any response or amendment filed prior to the first Office action) are premature and will be returned and not considered (37 CFR 1.939). Any petition requesting merger of reexamination with reexamination or reissue, or a stay filed prior to the order to reexamine, will be returned and not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183, the matter should be addressed in OPLA for decision. CRU Director or Reexamination Legal Advisor will return papers when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response too long — page limit enforcement (37 CFR 1.943)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the length of a patent owner or third party submission exceeds that permitted by 37 CFR 1.943, the submission is improper and a Notice will be mailed permitting the party to either (A) submit a redrafted response not exceeding page limit, or (B) file a copy with pages redacted to satisfy the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice sets a 15-day period to respond. If no response, the improper submission will not be considered and, if necessary to respond to an outstanding Office action, the reexamination prosecution may be terminated (1.957(b)) or limited (1.957(c)). Exceptions: table of contents, table of case law pages, and pages of the claims (but not claim charts) are excluded from the 30-page count. Affidavits/declarations containing arguments count toward the page limit; purely evidentiary exhibits generally do not unless they include argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper patent owner response frequency (one filing under 1.951(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner can only file once under 37 CFR 1.951(a). Any second or supplemental submission after Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) by the patent owner will be returned, unless prosecution has been reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2672 for additional handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party premature comments and scope limits (37 CFR 1.947)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comments filed by a third party requester subsequent to the request for reexamination and prior to the first Office action are premature and will be returned and will not be considered. Comments following the patent owner’s response to a first Office action must be limited to issues covered by the first action and/or the patent owner’s response; otherwise they will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third party files comments where the patent owner has not responded to the outstanding Office action, they are premature (37 CFR 1.947).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art submissions by third party requester must meet narrow criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For any third party requester comments containing a submission of prior art, the prior art must be limited solely to prior art which is necessary to (1) rebut a finding of fact by the examiner, (2) rebut a response of the patent owner, or (3) which for the first time became known or available to the third party requester after the filing of the request for inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art submitted as newly known must be accompanied by a statement when it first became known/available to the third party and include discussion of pertinency of each reference to patentability of at least one claim. If these criteria are not met, the comments are improper and will be returned (see MPEP § 2666.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental third party comments generally improper with limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental third party requester comments are improper since 37 CFR 1.947 states that comments can 'once' be filed; such supplemental comments are improper, will not be considered, and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: supplemental third party comments are permitted in response to the patent owner’s completion of a response (even if initial third party comments were provided after an incomplete patent owner response), and are permitted in response to a supplemental patent owner response. The third party requester can only respond to a patent owner submission after ACP and may only do so once under 37 CFR 1.951(b). Any original third party comments after ACP or any second/supplemental responsive comments after ACP are improper and will be returned (see MPEP § 2672).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper petitions and limitations on iterative oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay a reexamination proceeding because of an interference filed prior to the first Office action in the reexamination proceeding will be returned and not considered (37 CFR 1.939). Petitions by a third party not a party to an interference will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After an opposition to any petition is filed by a third party requester (regardless of entry rights), any further paper in opposition/rebuttal/response to that opposition will not be considered and will be returned. The same limitation applies to oppositions to patent owner petitions. There must be a limitation on party iterations given statutory mandate for special dispatch in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions by third parties other than the third party requester are limited
rubrics_metrics.description: No submissions on behalf of any third parties other than third party requesters as defined in 35 U.S.C. 100(e) will be considered unless such submissions are in accordance with 37 CFR 1.915 or are one of the exceptions noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted submissions by other third parties are limited to (1) a 37 CFR 1.501 art citation limited to patents and printed publications with explanation of pertinency and applicability, or (2) bare notice of suits and other proceedings involving the patent; such submissions must be without additional comment and cannot include further arguments or information. Improper submissions will be returned or destroyed. A proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission filed after the order to reexamine will be stored in the storage area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective papers retained in reexamination file — unsigned and no proof of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by the patent owner which are unsigned, or signed by less than all patent owners where no attorney/agent is of record, will be denied consideration but retained in the file (37 CFR 1.33). Papers filed without required proof of service may be denied consideration where it cannot be determined that service was in fact made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial of consideration in these circumstances affects timing rights (e.g., third party response/comment/appeal/brief periods) and may be treated accordingly (see 37 CFR 1.248 and MPEP § 2666.06).
